question.:question/problem: Which of the following is an upper triangular matrix?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that $A$ is a matrix for which all entries *below* the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Hence, it is an upper triangular matrix. 

By contrast, matrices $B$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ each have at least one non-zero entry below the diagonal:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & 6 \\ -7 & -2 & -7 \\ -8 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 7 \\ 9 & -7\end{aligned}],\,E=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -8 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

So, they are not upper triangular matrices.
